packing: Reef/water shoes: Ionian beaches are pebble (Myrtos, Antisamos) and the coves have rocky entries.
Snorkels + goggles: the Blue Caves swim stop, Fiskardo coves, and Antisamos headlands reward them.
Swim + sun kit: suits, UPF shirts, hats, and reef-safe sunscreen for long boat and beach days.
Motion-sickness backup: for the open Zakynthos crossing and the Meganisi cruise.
A light layer for the caves: Drogarati is a cool ~18°C even on a hot day.

days.heading: Depart Pittsburgh after work

facts.label: Constraint
facts.valueHtml: In Pittsburgh all day Jun 24-26; Jun 23 return is allowed

days.note: PIT has no nonstop to Greece and neither island airport takes long-haul, so the plan routes through a US gateway and Athens. Crucially, the Athens–Kefalonia leg can be single-ticketed through on Delta/Aegean or United/Aegean — so the arrival is on the reliable, well-served airport, not the thin one.

days.heading: Arrive Kefalonia (EFL), settle Sami

facts.label: Transfer
facts.valueHtml: EFL -> Sami ~35-45 min by rental car

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Collect the car, check in, grocery run, harbour dinner

days.note: Land at Kefalonia’s reliable airport, pick up the first rental car, and drive to a calm east-coast base near Sami — central to the caves, Myrtos, and the ferry. An easy grocery-and-taverna evening to shake off the flights.

spots.name: Land at Kefalonia (EFL) and settle on the Sami coast
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · kefaloniaIG · ionianseaIG · greeceFlickr

images.alt: White limestone rocks framing an electric-turquoise cove with Agia Efimia village at the mountain base, Kefalonia
Aerial looking down a limestone cliff into deep blue Ionian water meeting a rocky point
A catamaran silhouetted against a fiery sun setting over calm Ionian waters

spots.cost: Kefalonia Airport (EFL) is the reliable Ionian gateway — around 28 flights a week from Athens (Aegean and Sky Express, ~1h15), which can be single-ticketed through from the US on Delta/Aegean or United/Aegean. Pick up the first rental car at the airport (~9 min from Argostoli) and drive ~35–45 min to a Sami or Agia Efimia base on the calm east coast, central to the caves, Myrtos, and the ferry.
spots.climate: Ionian June: warm, dry, and calm. Highs ~78–84°F, sea a swimmable ~72–74°F, and only ~1–3 rain days all month. Mornings are glassy; a gentle NW Maistro breeze builds in the afternoon — nothing like the Aegean Meltemi. A grocery run tonight (there are Lidl/AB supermarkets in Argostoli and Sami) sets up easy apartment breakfasts.
spots.saveHtml: Save Base in Sami/Agia Efimia rather than pricier Fiskardo or Lassi; a self-catering apartment with a pool and an early grocery stop cuts the food line hard.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A first-night seafront taverna dinner in Agia Efimia while the kids decompress from the flights.
spots.restoHtml:
• Tereza, Sami — harbourfront pizza/café, a reliable plain-cheese-pizza landing spot after travel
  • Contessina Pizzeria, Sami — seaside pizza with a harbour view
  • Local AB / Lidl, Argostoli — stock the apartment for breakfasts and beach lunches
spots.altboxHtml:
• Base in Lassi instead for sandy, shallow beaches right by the airport if you prefer town amenities.
  • Quiet Agia Efimia harbour for a smaller-village feel with tavernas on the water.
  • Early night, no plans — the caves and Myrtos keep until tomorrow.

days.heading: Myrtos + Assos

facts.label: Swim rule
facts.valueHtml: Swim at calm Assos, not steep-shelved Myrtos

days.note: The postcard day: the Myrtos cliff-road panorama and a careful dip, then lunch and a gentle swim in the sheltered bay at pastel Assos below its Venetian castle. The two pair naturally on one north-coast loop.

spots.name: Myrtos Beach from the cliff road
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · myrtosIG · myrtosbeachIG · kefaloniaFlickr

images.alt: Myrtos Beach's white crescent and deep blue bay seen from the cliff road above, Kefalonia
A lone swimmer where turquoise shallows meet deep blue water at Myrtos Beach, Kefalonia
Cliff-top panorama of Myrtos Beach's white crescent and layered turquoise-to-navy water, Kefalonia

spots.cost: The island’s signature view — a white-pebble crescent between limestone headlands — and it’s free. Park at the northern clifftop viewpoint for the postcard panorama with the hairpin road in frame, then drive the steep switchbacks down to the sand. Free roadside/lot parking above the beach (arrive before ~10am in season); a set of sunbeds runs about €15/day.
spots.climate: Stunning to look at, tricky to swim. The seabed shelves steeply just metres out and waves/currents build with the afternoon breeze — multiple sources call it unsuitable for young or weak swimmers. Treat it as a wade-and-photograph beach for the 8-year-old and keep swimming close to shore; save real family swims for calmer Assos, Antisamos, or Lassi.
spots.saveHtml: Save The northern viewpoint is the shot — you can get the whole trip’s marquee photo without paying for anything but time. Bring your own shade and water rather than renting sunbeds.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A late-afternoon return for golden light on the white cliffs after the midday buses leave, with a drink at the viewpoint kantina.
spots.restoHtml:
• Alaties / Divino taverna, Agia Efimia — simple grilled chicken and pasta on the way back
  • Assos village tavernas — pair Myrtos with lunch in Assos (below)
  • Apartment picnic — there are no real facilities at the beach itself; pack lunch
spots.altboxHtml:
• Assos first, Myrtos viewpoint after for better afternoon light on the bay.
  • Skip the descent and enjoy the viewpoint only if the sea is rough — the swim isn’t the point here.
  • Combine with Fiskardo on a single north-coast loop day if pressed for time.

spots.name: Assos: a pastel village under a Venetian castle
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · assosIG · assoskefaloniaIG · kefaloniaFlickr

images.alt: Assos village's pastel houses on the narrow isthmus with the Venetian castle headland and turquoise bay, Kefalonia
Assos village's colorful houses wrapping a turquoise harbor with moored boats, Kefalonia
Pastel yellow, pink, and white Venetian-style houses lining the waterfront in Assos, Kefalonia

spots.cost: One of Greece’s prettiest villages: pastel houses on a slim isthmus below a pine-covered headland crowned by a 16th-century Venetian castle. Two free car parks (the near one fills first; the overflow is a ~5-min walk). The castle loop is a free ~2-hour walk (mostly unshaded — hats and water). The protected village bay is smooth pebbles and calm turquoise — the gentle family swim Myrtos isn’t.
spots.climate: Sheltered, calm, and easy. The horseshoe harbour bay stays gentle even when the open coast is choppy, with a soft pebble entry — ideal for the 8-year-old after the drama of Myrtos. June air in the low 80s°F; shade is scarce on the castle path, so do it early or late.
spots.saveHtml: Save Park in the free overflow lot and swim off the village bay for nothing; the castle walk is free and the best thing here anyway.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A long lunch at a harbourside taverna table right on the water, then the full castle-headland loop for the view back over the village.
spots.restoHtml:
• Platanos, Assos — waterfront taverna with pasta and grilled options for the kids
  • Molos / Nefeli, Assos — harbour tavernas with simple plates and village charm
  • Ice cream on the quay — a low-drama treat after the castle climb
spots.altboxHtml:
• Swim first, castle after to beat the midday heat on the unshaded path.
  • Skip the full castle loop with tired legs — the gate and lower walls still give the view.
  • Myrtos viewpoint on the same loop — the two pair naturally in one north-coast day.

days.heading: Melissani + Drogarati caves

facts.label: Timing
facts.valueHtml: Hit Melissani in the 11am-2pm sun window

days.note: A short, high-wow morning: the sunbeam-lit turquoise lake of Melissani by rowboat, timed for the midday sun shaft, then the cool stalactite cavern of Drogarati minutes away — a perfect heat-break, then an easy Sami swim.

spots.name: Melissani’s blue lake & Drogarati’s cavern
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · melissaniIG · melissanicaveIG · drogaratiFlickr

images.alt: Rowboats crossing Melissani Cave's turquoise underground lake beneath the collapsed round roof opening, Kefalonia
A wooden tour boat crossing Melissani Cave's glowing blue-green underground lake, Kefalonia
Golden-lit stalactite chamber deep inside Drogarati Cave near Sami, Kefalonia

spots.cost: Melissani is a collapsed-roof cave whose underground lake turns electric turquoise when the midday sun drops through the opening; a 10–15 min rowboat glides you across it. Admission is €10 adult / €5 child (a second on-site operator sets slightly different prices, so expect ±€3). A few minutes away, Drogarati is a big walk-in stalactite cavern — €6 adult / €3 child, or a €13 combo ticket. Summer hours ~09:00–19:00.
spots.climate: Time Melissani for 11am–2pm. The sunbeam that lights the water only fires when the sun is high, which also concentrates the crowds — arrive near opening of that window. Drogarati is a cool, dry ~18°C cavern, a good midday heat-break and easy for both kids (steps, no boat). Both are short visits, well suited to an 8-year-old’s attention span.
spots.saveHtml: Save Buy the €13 Melissani+Drogarati combo and go straight at the 11am sun window to skip the worst queue; the nearby Karavomilos lakeside park is a free shady picnic spot.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add a swim and lunch at Karavomilos or Sami afterwards, or a glass-bottom Sami boat trip to cap the cave morning.
spots.restoHtml:
• Karavomilos lake taverna — shaded tables by the spring, simple pasta and grills
  • Tereza / Contessina, Sami — harbour pizza a few minutes away
  • Melissani café kiosk — drinks and snacks between the two caves
spots.altboxHtml:
• Drogarati first, Melissani at the sun window to nail the blue-lake light.
  • Skip Drogarati if the kids have had enough — Melissani is the headliner.
  • Sami beach afterwards for an easy swim to finish the day.

days.heading: Fiskardo harbour day
days.note: The prettiest harbour on the island — the one village that survived the 1953 quake — with sheltered coves for easy swimming and optional self-drive boats to reach the clearest water. Do the picky-kid meal in Sami; Fiskardo dinner is the upscale splurge.

spots.name: Fiskardo: the Venetian harbour that survived the quake
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · fiskardoIG · fiscardoIG · kefaloniaFlickr

images.alt: A sailing yacht anchored in a turquoise cove near Fiskardo, Kefalonia
Yachts moored in Fiskardo harbor with pastel Venetian houses lining the waterfront, Kefalonia
Colorful Venetian-style waterfront houses and a moored fishing boat in Fiskardo village, Kefalonia

spots.cost: The one village that survived Kefalonia’s 1953 earthquake intact, so its pastel Venetian waterfront is the real thing — a compact, walkable harbour ringed with tavernas and lined with yachts. Wandering and swimming off the nearby coves is free; the splurge is a self-drive day boat (small rental boats sit right on the harbour, roughly €80–150/day for a licence-free outboard) to reach the turquoise coves.
spots.climate: Calm, sheltered east-coast water. The coves around Fiskardo (Emblisi, Foki) are protected and clear — easy family swimming with pine shade. June is warm and dry; the harbour is at its best in the early evening when the day boats return and the waterfront lights come on.
spots.saveHtml: Save Park on the edge and walk in; swim at free Emblisi or Foki cove just outside the village rather than renting a boat, and eat pizza in Sami before or after.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Rent a small self-drive boat for a half-day of cove-hopping, then a harbourfront seafood dinner at Irida or Tassia as the parents’-choice night.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pomodoro-style pizza in Sami/Agia Efimia — do the picky-kid meal off the harbour; Fiskardo skews upscale-seafood
  • Irida, Fiskardo — well-loved harbour taverna for the splurge dinner
  • Snack kiosks on the quay — crepes and ice cream keep the kids happy while parents linger
spots.altboxHtml:
• Emblisi or Foki cove for the swim instead of a boat rental.
  • Half-day only, paired with Assos/Myrtos on the north loop.
  • Water taxi to a cove if you skip driving a boat yourself.

days.heading: Antisamos beach day
days.note: The easy beach day: a wide, organised, green-backed bay minutes from Sami with sunbeds, tavernas, and gentle turquoise water for both kids — a relaxed counterpoint to wild Myrtos and a good mid-trip reset.

spots.name: Antisamos: a green-backed turquoise bay
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · antisamosIG · antisamosbeachIG · kefaloniaFlickr

images.alt: Antisamos Beach's turquoise water and white pebble shore backed by green pine-covered mountains, Kefalonia
Sailboats anchored below the green mountain backdrop of Antisamos Beach, Kefalonia
Antisamos Beach's turquoise-to-navy water framed by steep pine-green mountains, Kefalonia

spots.cost: A wide white-pebble bay backed by steep green pine hills (a Captain Corelli filming location), ~4km east of Sami. Free to visit; well organised with sunbeds and mattresses (~€15/pair, or free if you eat/drink at the beach bars), two tavernas, and good snorkelling just offshore. A genuine easy resort-day counterpart to wild Myrtos.
spots.climate: Calm, clear, and family-easy. Sheltered by its bay, the water is turquoise and gentle near shore, deepening gradually — comfortable for both kids in the ~73°F Ionian. It gets busy in high summer thanks to the film fame; a mid-morning arrival gets the best sunbeds before the tour crowd.
spots.saveHtml: Save Buy a couple of drinks at a beach bar to get free loungers, and bring snorkels — the rocky ends have the best fish for the kids.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A long lunch under the trees at the beach taverna, then a lazy full afternoon of swimming and snorkelling.
spots.restoHtml:
• Antisamos beach tavernas — grilled chicken, fries, and pasta right on the sand
  • Tereza / Contessina, Sami — the go-to pizza a few minutes away
  • Sami gelato — a harbour treat on the way home
spots.altboxHtml:
• Sami town beach for an easier, closer swim if legs are tired.
  • Snorkel the rocky headlands at either end for the best marine life.
  • Rest/pool afternoon — a slow beach day is a valid mid-trip reset.

days.heading: Zakynthos boat day

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Full-day boat: Blue Caves swim + Navagio view

facts.label: Honest
facts.valueHtml: Navagio cove is view-only (closed to landing)

days.note: The big set-piece: a full-day boat across to Zakynthos for the glowing Blue Caves (a real in-water swim stop) and the famous Navagio shipwreck cove — viewed from the bay mouth, since landing is closed. Book an early, calmer departure.

spots.name: Navagio (Shipwreck) viewpoint, Zakynthos
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · navagioIG · shipwreckbeachIG · zakynthosFlickr

images.alt: Aerial view of Navagio Shipwreck Beach's rusted wreck on white sand in a turquoise cove ringed by pale cliffs, Zakynthos
Cliff-top aerial of Navagio Beach's shipwreck and turquoise cove with tour boats crossing the electric-blue water, Zakynthos
Wide aerial of the Navagio shipwreck cove framed by pine trees and a deep blue-to-turquoise water gradient, Zakynthos

spots.cost: The most famous beach in Greece — a rusted wreck on white sand in a cliff-ringed turquoise cove. Honest status: the cove has been closed to landing and swimming through at least Oct 2026 after repeated landslides, so tour boats now view it from the bay mouth only, and the sanctioned land view is the clifftop platform above (reached via Volimes). Re-check the 2027 status before booking. A full-day Kefalonia–Zakynthos boat trip runs ~€45–60pp.
spots.climate: A long, sun-exposed sea day — morning is calmer. Book an early departure before the afternoon Maistro builds a little chop, bring hats, sunscreen, and motion-sickness backup for the open crossing. The boat still swims at other Zakynthos coves even though Navagio itself is view-only.
spots.saveHtml: Save Take the combined Blue Caves + Navagio-viewpoint boat rather than separate trips; it swims at open coves along the way, giving the kids water time even with the cove closed.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A smaller-group or semi-private boat with lunch included for more swim stops and less waiting.
spots.restoHtml:
• Onboard / packed lunch — most day boats include or allow food; pack kid snacks
  • Agia Efimia taverna dinner — back on Kefalonia after the boat
  • Ice cream at the harbour — a reliable end-of-boat-day win
spots.altboxHtml:
• Skip Zakynthos entirely if a long boat day sounds like too much — a Kefalonia beach day is a fair swap.
  • Blue Caves focus (below) for the best in-water swimming without the long Navagio run.
  • Clifftop platform by car+ferry only if you want the land view — it’s a big day for a photo.

spots.name: The Blue Caves by boat
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · bluecavesIG · zakynthosIG · ionianFlickr

images.alt: A tour boat entering a glowing electric-blue sea cave arch at Zakynthos's Blue Caves
A sunlit natural rock arch at Zakynthos's Blue Caves with luminous teal water beneath white cliffs

spots.cost: On Zakynthos’s north tip, a run of sea arches and grottoes where the water glows an unreal electric blue as light reflects off the white limestone below. Unaffected by the Navagio closure, so the boat actually goes in and stops to swim — the real in-water highlight of the day. Included in the same ~€45–60pp full-day boat trip.
spots.climate: Clear, cool, luminous water. The grottoes are calmest in the morning; the boat noses into the arches and usually gives a swim stop in the glowing water — a genuine wow for the kids. Bring goggles; the light is brightest under a high sun.
spots.saveHtml: Save It’s bundled into the day-boat fare — no extra cost. Bring your own goggles/snorkels rather than renting onboard.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A boat that lingers longer at the caves with a dedicated swim stop, or a sea-kayak add-on for the older kid.
spots.restoHtml:
• Onboard lunch — part of most full-day tours
  • Agios Nikolaos (Zak) kiosk — snacks near the north-tip departure coves
  • Kefalonia dinner — eat back at base after the crossing
spots.altboxHtml:
• Blue Caves only as a shorter northern-Zakynthos boat if the full day is too long.
  • Snorkel the swim stop for the best of the glowing water.
  • Swap for a Kefalonia cove day if seas are up.

days.heading: Argostoli + Lassi
days.feel: Turtles, the stone bridge, and sandy beaches

facts.label: Afternoon
facts.valueHtml: Shallow, sandy Makris/Platys Gialos at Lassi

days.note: A gentle last Kefalonia day: wild loggerhead turtles in Argostoli harbour, the historic De Bosset bridge over Koutavos lagoon, then the soft-sand, shallow Lassi beaches — the easiest swimming on the island for the 8-year-old. Repack tonight for the ferry.

spots.name: Argostoli: loggerhead turtles & the Lassi beaches
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · argostoliIG · koutavosIG · lassiFlickr

images.alt: A loggerhead sea turtle gliding over fish in Argostoli's clear harbor water, Kefalonia
A loggerhead sea turtle surfacing in Argostoli harbor's green-blue water, Kefalonia

spots.cost: The capital, and a gentle last Kefalonia day. Wild loggerhead sea turtles gather in the harbour (best 8–11am when the fishing boats return) — free to watch from the quay. Walk the 1813 De Bosset stone bridge across Koutavos lagoon, see the Katavothres sea-sinkholes, then finish at the shallow, sandy Lassi beaches (Makris Gialos / Platys Gialos) that are made for young kids (sunbeds ~€15–20/pair, lifeguard in peak season).
spots.climate: The easiest swimming on the island. Unlike pebbly steep Myrtos, Lassi’s Makris and Platys Gialos are soft sand with shallow, calm water a long way out — explicitly good for the 8-year-old. June is warm; the turtle-watch works best early, before the heat and the boats stir the harbour.
spots.saveHtml: Save Watch the turtles from the free public quay (no boat needed), walk the free De Bosset bridge, and bring your own beach shade for Lassi.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A sit-down waterfront lunch in Argostoli with a kids’ menu, then paid loungers at Makris Gialos for a lazy final beach afternoon.
spots.restoHtml:
• Ampelaki, Argostoli — waterfront taverna with a dedicated kids’ menu and plain pasta
  • Pizza Al Forno, Argostoli — homemade pizza since 2006, a solid picky-kid pick
  • Lassi beach bars — fries, toasties, and ice cream on the sand
spots.altboxHtml:
• Respect the turtles — watch, don’t feed or chase; the marine group posts guidance on the quay.
  • Platys over Makris for the volleyball court and a slightly quieter stretch.
  • Katavothres + lighthouse loop for a short novelty walk before the beach.

days.heading: Ferry to Lefkada, settle Nydri

facts.label: Transfer
facts.valueHtml: Fiskardo -> Vasiliki ferry ~1h, then ~40 min drive

facts.label: Swap
facts.valueHtml: Return the Kefalonia car; pick up a Lefkada car

days.note: The one inter-island move, and an easy one: a direct ~1-hour ferry from Fiskardo to Vasiliki, a fresh rental car, and a scenic drive up the Lefkada east coast to a Nydri base. Reconfirm the sailing time — the 2027 timetable isn’t published yet.

spots.name: Ferry the channel to Lefkada
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · ionianferryIG · fiskardoIG · lefkadaFlickr

images.alt: Sailboats and windsurfers skimming the turquoise waters of Vasiliki Bay, Lefkada
A red Odysseus-style tour boat with a painted eye anchored in a shallow turquoise cove below a green cliff on Lefkada's east coast

spots.cost: The one inter-island move, and it’s short: a direct Ionion Pelagos ferry Fiskardo (Kefalonia) → Vasiliki (Lefkada), about an hour across the channel, no Ithaca transfer needed. Roughly €40 for the car plus ~€11–12/adult and half-fare kids — about €90 for the family. Return the Kefalonia car at Fiskardo/EFL and pick up a fresh Lefkada car at Vasiliki, then drive up to a Nydri base (~40 min).
spots.climate: A calm, scenic hour. June crossings run a few times daily (frequency ramps up through the month); the channel is usually gentle in the morning. The exact 2027 timetable isn’t published yet — treat the schedule as a proxy and reconfirm on Ionion Pelagos/Ferryhopper before travel.
spots.saveHtml: Save Rent a separate economy car on each island (round-trip pickup at each) rather than paying a steep one-way ferry-crossing fee to carry one car across.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Time a mid-morning sailing and stop for lunch on the Vasiliki waterfront before driving up the Lefkada east coast.
spots.restoHtml:
• Vasiliki waterfront tavernas — simple pasta and grills at the arrival port
  • Pomodoro, Nydri — wood-fired pizza waiting at the new base
  • Ferry snacks — pack drinks/snacks; onboard options are limited
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lower-risk variant: round-trip EFL — fly in and out of Kefalonia and reach Lefkada by this same ferry both ways, trading one extra crossing for avoiding the thin PVK flight.
  • Book the ferry ahead in peak weeks for the car deck.
  • Early sailing to keep the afternoon for settling in at Nydri.

days.heading: West-coast beaches

facts.label: Holiday
facts.valueHtml: Juneteenth observed Fri Jun 18 - a no-PTO active day

facts.label: Timing
facts.valueHtml: Go early: west beaches chop up in the afternoon wind

days.note: On the Juneteenth observed holiday (no PTO for many employers), tackle Lefkada’s famous white-cliff west coast in the calm morning: the postcard cliffs of Porto Katsiki and the easy, organised sands of Kathisma, with boat-only Egremni viewed from the water.

spots.name: Porto Katsiki & the west-coast beaches
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · portokatsikiIG · egremniIG · lefkadaFlickr

images.alt: Aerial view of Porto Katsiki's curving white beach and turquoise cove, Lefkada
Egremni Beach's white cliffs framing a turquoise cove with a sea arch, Lefkada
A wildflower hillside dropping to a rock-dotted turquoise cove near Kathisma beach, Lefkada
Aerial of rows of blue sunbed umbrellas on golden sand meeting turquoise surf on Lefkada's west coast

spots.cost: Lefkada’s west coast is a run of white-cliff, turquoise-water beaches. Porto Katsiki is the postcard — ~80–100 steps down from a paid clifftop lot (~€8–15/day, half-price after 4pm; no beach fee). Kathisma is the big, easy, organised beach (free lot, sunbeds, tavernas) — the family-friendly pick. Egremni is currently boat-only after a June 2025 municipal closure of the land route (re-verify for 2027); day boats reach it from Nydri/Vasiliki.
spots.climate: Go in the morning. These west-facing beaches are calm at dawn, but the NW Maistro builds from midday and brings real chop and bigger waves by afternoon — every source says visit early for calm water and a parking spot. Kathisma is the most sheltered and stroller-friendly; Porto Katsiki’s steep climb is hot at midday.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do Kathisma (free parking, sunbeds, easy access) as the main swim and Porto Katsiki as a morning photo-and-dip; skip paid sunbeds and bring shade.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A boat trip from Vasiliki/Nydri that reaches Porto Katsiki and boat-only Egremni from the water, avoiding the cliff stairs entirely.
spots.restoHtml:
• Rachi, Exanthia — famous sunset-view taverna above the west coast, simple options for kids
  • Kathisma beach bars — fries, toasties, and pasta right on the sand
  • Pack water + snacks — Porto Katsiki has only a small kantina
spots.altboxHtml:
• Kathisma over Porto Katsiki if the kids won’t do the cliff stairs.
  • Kavalikefta for a quieter, wilder west-coast cove (narrow access road).

days.note: A change of pace: the pretty car-free village of Agios Nikitas and a water-taxi hop to Milos beach in the calm morning, then south to windsurf-famous Vasiliki bay where the older kid can try a beginner lesson on the reliable afternoon wind.

images.alt: Agios Nikitas village rooftops and stone lanes dropping to its turquoise cove beneath a forested headland, Lefkada

spots.cost: Agios Nikitas is Lefkada’s prettiest, car-free stone village — walkable lanes and easy tavernas. Just around the headland, Milos beach is reached on foot (15–20 min uphill each way, past an old windmill) or by a ~5-min water taxi (~€5–10pp) — the easier call with kids. Down south, Vasiliki bay is a windsurf mecca; the 13-year-old can try a beginner lesson on the reliable afternoon wind.
spots.climate: Village mornings, wind sports afternoons. Milos and the west side are calmest before midday; Vasiliki is the opposite — flat and calm early, then a dependable ~15–20kt thermal wind fills in around 3pm (which is exactly why windsurfers love it). Schedule family swims in the morning and any windsurf lesson for the afternoon.
spots.saveHtml: Save Walk to Milos beach instead of the water taxi if the kids are up for the uphill return; wander Agios Nikitas and swim off the village beach for free.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A beginner windsurf lesson at Vasiliki for the older kid, and a sunset dinner in car-free Agios Nikitas.
spots.restoHtml:

  • Agios Nikitas village tavernas — simple fish, pasta, and grills in the car-free lanes
  • Vasiliki waterfront — casual lunch between windsurf sessions
spots.altboxHtml:

  • Kids’ windsurf/SUP at Vasiliki on the afternoon wind.

days.note: The Lefkada boat day from Nydri: motoring into the Papanikolis sea cave and around the old Onassis islands with turquoise swim stops — sheltered and gentle for the kids — with the shaded Dimosari gorge as a cool-off alternative if you want land time.

Aerial view straight down on a sailboat and dinghy floating on vivid turquoise water off Lefkada

spots.cost: From Nydri harbour, a wooden day-boat cruises the Meganisi channel: the boat motors inside the Papanikolis sea cave (a real kid wow), then loops the former Onassis islands of Skorpios and Madouri with a turquoise swim stop — roughly €30–40pp for a group cruise, ~€70–80pp with lunch. Pair a morning gorge or afternoon boat: the free Dimosari gorge walk near Nydri is a short, shaded canyon (parking free), though the falls run low by June — treat it as a pretty walk, not a waterfall swim.
spots.climate: Calm channel, shaded gorge. The Meganisi/Skorpios cruise is sheltered and gentle — good for the 8-year-old — with warm ~73°F swim stops in turquoise coves. The Dimosari gorge is shaded and cool, a fine hot-afternoon alternative, but manage expectations on the waterfall flow by mid-June.
spots.saveHtml: Save Take the group wooden-boat cruise (not a private charter) and bring your own snacks; the Dimosari gorge and its trailhead parking are free.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A smaller-group Meganisi cruise with lunch and more swim stops, or a private boat to time the Papanikolis cave without crowds.
spots.restoHtml:

  • Nydri waterfront tavernas — grills and simple plates along the harbour
  • The Plane Tree, Dimosari trailhead — drinks/snacks at the gorge entrance
spots.altboxHtml:
• Boat only if the gorge is dry — the Meganisi cruise is the real highlight.
  • Dimosari gorge morning, boat afternoon, or vice versa.
  • Sivota bay lunch by boat or car for another turquoise cove.

days.note: A relaxed finale: walkable Lefkada Town, the floating causeway, and the flat lagoon loop past the Gyra windmills, with a last waterfront dinner. Repack tonight — the causeway puts Preveza airport just a short drive away tomorrow.

spots.name: Lefkada Town, the lagoon & Gyra windmills
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · lefkadatownIG · gyraIG · lefkadaFlickr

images.alt: Lefkada Town's waterfront promenade with cafe umbrellas, sailboat masts, and bougainvillea
Sun flare over the weathered stone windmill at Gyra beach beside the Lefkada lagoon

spots.cost: An easy, free last day. Lefkada Town connects to the mainland by the Agia Mavra floating causeway (no ferry ever needed to reach the island), and its centre is walkable and full of casual tavernas. The flat ~7km Gyra loop path rings the western lagoon past the surviving stone windmills and Gyra beach — a relaxed bike or drive-and-stroll to close the trip and repack before the short hop to Preveza airport.
spots.climate: Warm, flat, and shadeless around the lagoon. Walk or cycle the Gyra loop early or late; midday on the exposed spit is hot. The town itself has shaded lanes and a swing bridge that opens on the hour for boats — an easy, low-key finale after a busy Lefkada week.
spots.saveHtml: Save The whole day is essentially free — walk the town, the lagoon path, and Gyra beach, and eat a final pizza in the centre.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A last seafood dinner on the Lefkada Town waterfront, or a sunset drink out at the Gyra windmills.
spots.restoHtml:
• Made in Love, Lefkada Town — Neapolitan-trained pizzeria, family-friendly, gluten-free dough option
  • Lefkada Town centre tavernas — simple pasta, grills, and gyros in the walkable lanes
  • Bakeries + gelato — easy trailside snacks for the lagoon loop
spots.altboxHtml:
• Gyra beach swim for one last dip near town.
  • Bike the lagoon loop instead of driving for an active last morning.
  • Early repack — Preveza airport is only ~20–36 min via the causeway.

Timing and safety

  • West-coast beaches in the morning — afternoon wind brings chop.
  • Myrtos is a wade beach for young kids — steep shelf, waves.

What People Are Saying

Research signals to keep in mind

Operator data, official cave fees, and June climate all point the same way: the Ionian is the warm-and-easy swim pick, with one flight leg to manage.

Swim signal

June sea temps of ~72-74°F, the gentle Maistro breeze (no Meltemi), and sheltered coves at Assos, Antisamos, Lassi, and Milos all confirm the same thing: this is the board’s easiest warm-water week, with the marquee Myrtos best admired and calmer bays best swum.

Logistics signal

Kefalonia’s ~28 weekly Athens flights and Delta/Aegean interline make the arrival single-ticketable, and the direct ~1h Fiskardo-Vasiliki ferry keeps island-hopping simple — while the thin Preveza departure is the one leg reviewers flag as fragile.

Family signal

The Melissani boat, the Blue Caves swim, the Papanikolis cave cruise, the Argostoli turtles, and shallow sandy Lassi are the wins for an 8-year-old; the 13-year-old gets a Vasiliki windsurf lesson, snorkelling, and the cliff-beach adventure.
